papers.title: LPT: Orchestrating bounded agentic loops for automated protein binder design
papers.summary: Current large language models (LLMs) can reason over scientific information and use code-based tools, but their training knowledge is broad rather than specialized, can be out of date and is hard to attribute to sources. Furthermore, unconstrained agentic workflows and unlimited tool use can consume large amounts of tokens. Here we present LPT (little protein tiger), a framework for fixed orchestration of LLM stages, each running a bounded agentic loop with custom system prompts and tool access, to enable de novo protein binder design from a single natural language prompt. The LLM stages can query a curated literature database, containing ~14000 papers digested into key findings, enabling recall of specialized information. An LLM with database access answered 41/48 test questions drawn from database key findings correctly, while a model without access answered none. In three end-to-end design campaigns, initiated from a single prompt, LPT autonomously identified the design intent, selected targets, structures and hotspot residues and designed candidate binders to disrupt CALCRL/RAMP1, PD-1/PD-L1 and PVR-TIGIT interactions. Cross-validation with multiple folding models confirms a high in silico success rate at minimal token consumption and low computational costs.

papers.title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems: Prior Scores Compromise Evaluation Independence
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assess generated content, giving rise to the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm. These systems now score outputs, filter content, and gate iterative refinement in production pipelines, where each judgment is often assumed to be independent of earlier evaluations. We test this assumption using three prompt conditions: no metadata, revision framing, and anchored metadata containing revision, attempt, and prior-score fields. We show that prior scores, even when included only as context metadata, anchor judgments and systematically shift ratings toward their values. Across 192,000 attempted evaluations (185,271 successful), seven out of the eight evaluated models have 95% task-stratified bootstrap intervals below zero for the total anchored-metadata effect on 20 fixed texts. Cohen's $d$, a standardized measure of the difference between score distributions, reaches an absolute value of 0.71. Token-level analysis of selected model-task probes suggests a threshold-like response pattern: introducing anchored metadata produces a marked redistribution of output-score probabilities, while changing the anchor value within the tested below-threshold range produces comparatively little additional variation. papers.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
papers.summary: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query-tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent.

papers.title: PTMD Defensive Publication and Universal AI/LLM Open-Use Declaration
papers.summary: This document is a defensive publication and universal AI/LLM open-use declaration for the Prouhet–Thue–Morse–De Smet 396/237-Matrix (PTMD) framework developed by Luc De Smet and publicly described in The Book of Sovereignty: The 396-Code Algorithm, first published on 25 October 2026. Its purpose is to consolidate, clarify and make explicit the artificial-intelligence and computational applications already disclosed throughout the Book, while also placing those applications into a concise, searchable and citable technical record. The declaration covers the use of PTMD principles in large language models, multimodal models, reasoning systems, autonomous agents, multi-agent systems, symbolic and neuro-symbolic architectures, reinforcement-learning systems, embodied AI, simulated agents and future computational-intelligence architectures. Among the disclosed concepts are: PTM binary source grammar and recursive balance generation; the 1467|2358 polarity structure; the 9/11 decimal modular interface; the Root-of-37 cross-base boundary; the Radix Pyramid and cross-representation architecture; X/Y/Z generation-filter-memory structures; the 237 Source Bridge; the 273–237–396 Binary Bridge; the 1984 stress architecture; Hinge states; chooser architectures; the pauzeke or sovereign pause; provenance-aware reasoning; preservation of intermediate information; resonance and multi-path conv

papers.title: Persona Conditioning as an Assessor-Sensitivity Probe for LLM-Based IR Evaluation
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as relevance assessors in information retrieval (IR) evaluation, raising questions about how assessor framing affects judgment reliability and downstream system comparison. We study persona conditioning as a diagnostic mechanism for exposing LLM assessor sensitivity. Using task-oriented personas drawn from two complementary sources (PersonaHub and NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas-USA), we instantiate five assessor roles emphasizing intent interpretation, domain expertise, contrastive judgment, evidence verification, and global search-quality assessment, compared with a standard UMBRELA baseline. Across six LLM backbones on TREC DL20 and RAG24, our analyses reveal structured rather than uniform assessor sensitivity. Judgments usually remain close to the baseline while shifting assessment strictness, evidential threshold, or interpretation emphasis rather than producing widespread relevance reversals. At the system level, high-capacity models preserve system-ranking agreement, while smaller models amplify persona-induced instability. Local rank-displacement analysis shows sensitivity concentrates on particular retrieval systems and system types, especially neural ranking/reranking systems on DL20 and RAG-oriented pipelines on RAG24. Persona source matters less than assessor role and model capacity. These findings position persona-conditi

papers.title: Schema-Primed Knowledge-Augmented Approach to Water Injection Diagnostics and Closed-Loop Reservoir Dynamic Analysis
papers.summary: Abstract Water-injection diagnosis in a mature low-permeability waterflood is a longitudinal decision process. Engineers repeatedly identify anomalies, select interventions, and assess subsequent changes in waterflood performance indicators (WPIs), often over several years for one well. Existing knowledge-augmented language-model systems can answer individual questions but do not preserve the resulting engineering decision as a structured record for later evaluation. This study extends a schema-primed Knowledge-Augmented Generation (KAG) framework with persistent agentic memory for reservoir dynamic analysis. Before document ingestion, a petroleum domain ontology defines the admissible entity and relation types. Field reports, well files, and operational logs are then extracted into a typed graph. Each diagnostic session produces a typed record containing the diagnosis, recorded intervention, and expected WPI response. A later session retrieves that record and compares its expectation with production data the diagnosis never saw. The framework was evaluated at the Wangyao oilfield in the Ordos Basin, over 32.4 km². A 100-question reservoir-engineering benchmark was scored under two blinded model-based regimes, a gold-anchored judge repeated three times and a five-configuration expertise-anchored panel. The schema-primed KAG arm scored above vector-only and generic graph retriev

papers.title: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
papers.summary: Evolutionary coding agents such as AlphaEvolve are one of the notable successes in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to build AI Scientists. These agents tackle open-ended scientific problems by iteratively improving and evolving programs, leveraging the prior knowledge and reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Despite their success, mutations over programs are mostly low-level upon surface heuristics, without a persistent unit of control. In contrast, science compounds through ideas. In this work, we propose ExpEvolve, which injects idea-level extraction and control into evolution: it discovers and leverages the high-level factors from programs that explain scoring differences among different programs. We characterize theoretical conditions on when discovery with idea factors improves sample efficiency. We also build a practical framework to show that the extracted high-level idea factors are helpful for guiding exploitation from experience and exploration when discovery comes to a plateau. Across 11 open-ended mathematical tasks, ExpEvolve significantly improves the final performance and sample efficiency up to 5.0x. The improvements also transfer to 4 other LLMs and to 6 machine learning tasks from MLS-Bench. Analysis shows that ExpEvolve can discover idea-level factors to provide better exploration and exploitation for evolutionary discovery.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
papers.summary: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. Findings: Previous mathematics achievement had the strongest positive correlation with current mathematics performance, followed by mathematics se

papers.title: MUSE: An Interactive Meta-Agent for Understanding and Steering LLM-powered Data Science Systems
papers.summary: Recent advances in large language models have enabled a new class of agentic data science systems that allow users to complete complex data science workflows through natural language. Although these systems can significantly reduce manual effort, it remains difficult to diagnose their behavior and steer the reasoning process when failures or unexpected outputs occur. We present MUSE, an interactive meta-agent that enhances user understanding and control of agentic data science systems by (1) dynamically restructuring low-level execution traces into multiple semantic levels that support navigation from high-level overviews to low-level implementation details; (2) enabling users to reference specific workflow steps in context to ask grounded questions, provide feedback, and revise problematic steps without manually locating relevant execution history; and (3) supporting mixed-initiative steering by surfacing suspicious steps for inspection, scaffolding the repair process, and translating user repair intent into contextualized instructions for the underlying agent. In a between-subjects study (n = 15), MUSE improved task efficiency and increased users’ confidence in understanding and steering agentic data science workflows.

papers.title: Learning Calibrated Confidence for Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.summary: Complex information seeking on the Web often requires collecting evidence from multiple documents and reasoning across them, as in multi-hop question answering. Multi-agent systems address such tasks by dividing work among specialized agents, where upstream agents produce intermediate answers and supporting evidence that downstream agents build upon. However, upstream answers vary in correctness, and most systems provide no quantitative signal about it, leaving the downstream agent to judge whether to trust or verify what it receives based solely on the textual evidence. In this paper, we propose MASCAL. Each agent learns to produce a correctness probability for its answer by jointly optimizing task performance and confidence calibration in reinforcement learning; the upstream agent passes this probability at handoff, giving the downstream agent a quantitative basis for its decisions, and the final answer also carries a calibrated probability, quantifying the reliability of the system output. To guide the downstream agent in using this signal during training, we introduce confidence-aware weighting, which increases the learning weight at positions responsive to the upstream probability, so that the agent learns more from decisions where it actively uses the signal. Across three collaboration architectures spanning Web retrieval and reasoning tasks, MASCAL improves task accuracy

papers.title: Can We Rely on Language Models to Orchestrate Services across the Edge-Cloud Continuum?
papers.summary: Service orchestration across the edge--cloud continuum increasingly uses language models (LMs) to translate intents and operational evidence into scheduling, configuration, diagnosis, and remediation decisions. Yet, useful model outputs do not by themselves establish dependable orchestration: reliability also depends on where the LM enters the decision process, what authority it is granted, how actions are constrained, and what system-level evidence supports the claimed effect. Existing surveys provide limited synthesis of the links between continuum-specific orchestration decisions, LM responsibility, operational authority, assurance controls, and supporting empirical evidence. We systematically review 39 primary studies and develop a five-dimensional analytical framework for connecting system context, orchestration decisions, LM agency, operational safeguards, and evaluation evidence. The synthesis reveals predominantly hybrid designs in which LMs support interpretation, candidate generation, and mitigation planning, while downstream components commonly retain feasibility enforcement and execution authority. Bounded closed-loop remediation is emerging, but continuum-specific constraints remain unevenly represented in decision formulations, and production-scale evidence across heterogeneous edge--cloud environments remains limited. These findings suggest that reliance on LM-en

papers.title: Pre-Crime for Agents, at the Last Second: Probing When a Recruited Agent Gives In
papers.summary: When AI agents share channels and credentials, one agent can press another to break its operator's rule, a first step towards collusion. Output filters check only what an agent has already written. Can an overseer tell beforehand that an agent is about to give in? We show that a linear probe on the agent's activations can, in a controlled multi-agent setting. Across six scenarios, a peer presses a target for up to 20 rounds to reveal a secret, such as a deploy token; the target often refuses, then gives in. Read at each model call before its output is written, the probe picks out the one that leaks. On held-out Qwen3-32B episodes, at a threshold set to flag 5% of benign calls, it catches 82% of leaking calls. At a similar flag rate, a zero-shot decision-model monitor catches 26%. On gpt-oss-20b, a probe on its reasoning reaches AUROC 0.91. A bag-of-words classifier trained on the same calls comes close, so most of the gain comes from training on labels, not activations. The probe also flags permitted disclosures: it reads the coming disclosure more than the violation. The warning is short-range, and halting on any alarm would stop most benign episodes, which a second text check does not fix. A warning raised before generation could let an overseer stop an agent that is about to give in, ahead of others acting on its messages or recruitment spreading through a swarm.

papers.title: Before the Next Rollout: Diagnosing Skill Utility Shifts from Policy Updates
papers.summary: Skill-evolution methods typically analyze execution trajectories to guide agent skill refinement. However, policy updates can change the behavioral effects and marginal utility of an unchanged skill. Attribution based on earlier trajectories may therefore no longer reflect the skill's contribution under the updated policy. Moreover, trajectory failures can arise from multiple factors, making individual skill contributions difficult to isolate. We evaluate whether policy-update signals contain predictive information about changes in skill marginal utility. At fixed contexts from pre-update training rollouts, we measure how policy updates change the contrast in token preferences between skill and control conditions. Combining these interaction shifts with advantage estimates yields reward-directed readouts for diagnosing utility changes. The readouts reuse existing training rollouts and require only forward passes for single-step action scoring, without additional post-update rollout evaluation. Our experiments show that policy updates can alter skill marginal utility and that policy-update readouts carry diagnostic information for identifying skills with declining utility. Integrating readout-guided prioritization into skill evolution improves downstream performance while reducing policy and editor token consumption.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Profiling What Matters: Context-Aware Item Profiles from Large-Scale Metadata for LLM Recommenders
papers.summary: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced reranking in recommendation, effectively leveraging item-side information remains challenging. Real-world items are described by vast, heterogeneous, and unstructured metadata, where decision-relevant signals are often implicit, noisy, or buried in long descriptions. Moreover, feature salience is highly context-dependent, varying not only across items but also across users. Existing methods often rely on item titles, fixed attributes, or static item summaries, which limit personalized and fine-grained item understanding. To bridge this gap, we propose CAIRO, a user context-aware item profiling framework for LLM-based reranking. CAIRO first structures raw metadata and reviews into objective features and subjective traits, and employs a lightweight profiler to select the most relevant information for each user-item pair with limited serving-time overhead. The resulting profiles are concise and context-specific, providing relevant item-side evidence for the LLM's ranking decision. Experiments show that CAIRO consistently improves LLM-based reranking, highlighting the importance of item profiling that effectively exploits vast item-side information.

papers.title: Designing and Explaining an Entrepreneurship Model for Artificial Intelligence–Based Businesses
papers.summary: The primary objective of the present study was to design and explain an entrepreneurship model for artificial intelligence–based businesses, with a focus on the information and communications technology and computer software industries in knowledge-based companies located in Tehran Province. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of approach, it was a qualitative study employing a sequential exploratory design. In the qualitative phase, grounded theory was applied using the systematic approach to identify and conceptualize the dimensions, components, and relationships among the variables affecting AI-based entrepreneurship. The qualitative research field consisted of senior and middle managers, specialists, experts, and experienced employees working in the information and communications technology and computer software industries of knowledge-based companies in Tehran Province. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, which continued until theoretical saturation was reached. Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using MAXQDA 2024. To enhance the credibility and trustworthiness of the data, triangulation and Lincoln and Guba’s criteria, including credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability, were employed. The findings indicated that the entrepreneurship model for AI-based businesses con

papers.title: Deep learning integration of ultrasound perfusion and stiffness maps predicts tumor response to treatment
papers.summary: The complex tumor microenvironment and tumor heterogeneity make treatment responses highly variable, driving the shift toward biomarker-based therapy prediction. Ultrasound shear wave elastography (SWE) provides a simple and non-invasive method to measure tissue mechanical properties, such as tumor stiffness, by tracking shear wave propagation speed. Increased tumor stiffness is closely associated with compression of intratumoral blood vessels, which can severely limit blood flow within solid tumors, causing hypo-perfusion and hypoxia. These two abnormalities, in turn, hinder effective drug delivery and induce immunosuppression, which compromise the efficacy of cancer therapies. Tumor perfusion can be evaluated using contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), a minimally invasive imaging technique that employs microbubble contrast agents alongside ultrasound imaging to visualize blood flow and quantify tissue perfusion. In this study, we first developed CNN-ultra, a convolutional neural network trained separately on SWE and CEUS images to predict tumor response to chemo-immunotherapy in murine models of breast cancer, sarcoma, and melanoma. The dataset consisted of 587 SWE and CEUS images acquired prior to chemo-immunotherapy and tumor response was classified as responsive, stable, or non-responsive according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) adapted to volumet

papers.title: Generation of synthetic clinical text: a systematic review
papers.summary: Generating medical synthetic text represents an effective solution for clinical NLP issues like sparsity and privacy. This paper conducts a systematic review on synthetic clinical text generation by formulating quantitative analysis to three research questions concerning the generation’s purpose, generation techniques, and the evaluation methods. We searched four databases including PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Web of Science for publications associated with the topic and identified 87 relevant articles out of 1148. Results showed that the generation purposes were dedicated to Trustworthy, Medical Assistance, and Language Resource themes. Prompting LLMs was the main source of synthetic text (40 articles). GPTs were the main predominant technique used to generate the text (63 articles), especially ChatGPT (47 articles). Additionally, there were four main aspects of evaluation, including similarity, privacy, structure, and utility, where utility was the prevailing method for assessment (52 articles). The synthetic medical text empowered data augmentation and clinical documentation. Using text alteration, controlling real text portions, and federated learning, generative models can produce privacy-preserving medical text. This accelerates the development of new digital health applications.

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: Designing a Curriculum Model Based on Artificial Intelligence and Purposeful Physical Activity to Enhance Learning Self-Regulation, Mental Health, and Psychological Well-Being among Students
papers.summary: Objective: The objective of this study was to design and validate a curriculum model based on artificial intelligence and purposeful physical activity with emphasis on enhancing learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being among students. Methods and Materials: This applied developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, 20 experts in curriculum studies, educational technology, artificial intelligence in education, physical education, educational psychology, and student mental health were selected through purposive criterion-based sampling from Tehran and participated in semi-structured interviews. The interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis to extract the main dimensions, components, and indicators of the proposed curriculum model. In the quantitative phase, 384 secondary school students from Tehran were selected through multistage cluster sampling during the 2025–2026 academic year. Data were collected using a researcher-made curriculum model validation questionnaire, a learning self-regulation questionnaire, the General Health Questionnaire, and a psychological well-being scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. Findings: The inferential findings showed that the final curri

papers.title: LEMMA-RCA: A Large Multi-modal Multi-domain Dataset for Root Cause Analysis
papers.summary: Root cause analysis (RCA) is crucial for enhancing the reliability and performance of complex systems. However, progress in this field has been hindered by the lack of large-scale, open-source datasets tailored for RCA. To bridge this gap, we introduce LEMMA-RCA, a large dataset designed for diverse RCA tasks across multiple domains and modalities. LEMMA-RCA features various real-world fault scenarios from Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) systems, including microservices, water distribution, and water treatment systems, with hundreds of system entities involved. We evaluate the performance of six baseline methods on LEMMA-RCA across various settings, including offline and online models, as well as single and multi-modal settings. Our study demonstrates the utility of LEMMA-RCA in facilitating fair evaluation and promoting the development of more robust RCA techniques. The dataset is publicly available at https://www.lemmarca.info, with archival metadata and access instructions deposited under DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20516735.

papers.title: Spontaneous neuropathic pain
papers.summary: Spontaneous pain is a highly prevalent and disabling consequence of neuropathic disorders, yet it remains mechanistically underdefined and therapeutically underserved. Historically, preclinical animal models and clinical trials have been overwhelmingly biased toward stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity, relegating spontaneous pain to a secondary manifestation. Emerging evidence now challenges this view. Converging data from pharmacology, neural recordings, and systems-level causal manipulations indicate that spontaneous and stimulus-evoked pain arise from substantially dissociable molecular, cellular, and circuit substrates. Injured-fiber–derived ectopic activity within specific sensory neuron subtypes serves as a dominant peripheral generator of spontaneous pain, whereas cellularly distinct, intact spared-fiber pathways mediate stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity. At spinal and supraspinal levels, spontaneous pain preferentially engages affective–salience networks during pain chronification and may ultimately become stabilized within higher-order circuitry—while remaining dynamically coupled to afferent input. This mechanistic delineation carries critical translational implications. Current diagnostic and treatment guidelines rarely differentiate symptom domains, and most therapies have been validated primarily using stimulus-evoked or overall pain intensity endpoints—potentially con

papers.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
papers.summary: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. papers.title: From generation to judgment: the multidimensional structure of design thinking mindset and differences across learning stages in AIGC-supported fashion film design learning
papers.summary: Introduction Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is changing how design alternatives are generated in fashion film design learning, enabling students to obtain large numbers of comparable and iteratively refinable visual outcomes within a short period. However, expanded generative capacity does not, by itself, determine how learners interpret, evaluate, experiment with, and select among uncertain outcomes. In this human–AI collaborative creative environment, empirical evidence remains limited on whether learners’ design-related psychological tendencies form a distinguishable multidimensional structure that is comparable across learning stages. Design Thinking Mindset (DTM) provides a multidimensional psychological framework for addressing this issue. Methods Drawing on Vignoli et al.’s DTM framework, this study examined five dimensions—Uncertainty and Risk, Empathy, Experimentation, Abductive Reasoning, and Creative Confidence—through a cross-sectional survey of 409 first-year and third-year students from three Chinese universities who had experience with AIGC fashion film design projects. Confirmatory factor analysis and measurement invariance testing across year groups were used to examine the five-dimensional structure and its measurement comparability, followed by latent mean comparisons. papers.title: Reading–Writing Integration Through ChatGPT-Supported Feedback: Growth, Associations, and Mediated Pathways of Student Engagement in Chinese Classrooms
papers.summary: Abstract Although reading–writing integration has been increasingly advocated in Chinese language education, limited empirical evidence explains how reading, writing, and student engagement become integrated, particularly under AI-supported feedback. To address this issue, this study examined whether ChatGPT-supported feedback improved reading outcomes, writing outcomes, and student engagement, while investigating their interrelationships, the mediating role of student engagement, and the corresponding pathways in reading–writing integration. A total of 400 middle school students from eight intact classes in Shenzhen participated, with 200 students receiving ChatGPT-supported feedback and 200 receiving human-generated feedback. Using a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design, data were analyzed within a quantitative longitudinal framework integrating baseline equivalence tests, 2 × 2 mixed-design ANOVAs, factor-level correlation analyses, and multi-group cross-lagged path analysis to examine changes and temporal relationships among reading, student engagement, and writing across two groups (N = 400). Despite comparable pretest scores, findings showed that Group 1 demonstrated significantly greater pretest–posttest gains in reading, student engagement, and writing, with significant Time × Group interactions and large effects. papers.title: Rethinking digital twins in transportation: From virtual model to Human-in-the-Loop control
papers.summary: Digital twins have emerged as a transformative concept in many fields, traffic management including. Yet their definition and practical applications remain ambiguous. This paper seeks to clarify what constitutes a true digital twin, distinguishing it from traditional traffic simulation models, and explores scenarios where digital twins offer unique advantages. Drawing on global best practices and state-of-the-art research, we identify key challenges and provide actionable insights into their resolution. A pivotal contribution of this study is the introduction of the Digital Twin Evropská (DTE), a real-world case study focused on a critical urban corridor in Prague. We detail the motivation for its development, the methodologies employed, including real-time path-flow estimation, continuous simulation calibration, and integrated data-assimilation workflows, and the resulting insights. Under the taxonomy proposed in this paper, the currently implemented DTE is classified as a Digital Shadow with predictive capabilities, while the Human-in-the-Loop decision-support architecture represents the proposed pathway towards a fully operational Digital Twin. The findings demonstrate the practical utility of continuously synchronized digital representations for urban traffic management and provide a basis for their further development towards operational Digital Twins. papers.title: IntentLint: Supporting Intent Scaffolding and Prompt-time Linting in Human-AI Collaborative Data Analysis
papers.summary: In human-AI collaborative data analysis, as analyses rapidly evolve, the artifacts meant to capture shared understanding often become incomplete or difficult to interpret, leading to undocumented assumptions, cross-user misaligned intent, context-poor prompts, and unwanted agent behaviors. To address these challenges, we introduce a rule-based coordination layer with two interaction mechanisms, intent scaffolding and prompt-time linting, that make analytic intent explicit and actionable during human–AI collaborative data analysis. We implement them in IntentLint, a proof-of-concept system that infers analytic intent from shared notebooks, represents it as structured, editable rules, and checks users’ prompts against shared rules. IntentLint helps analysts externalize and refine their intent and proactively checks prompts for potential conflicts. A study with 16 data analysts shows that IntentLint improves awareness of collaborators’ intent and encourages reflection on analytic strategies, and provides design implications for supporting more aligned and transparent human-AI collaborative data analysis.

papers.title: Dialogic Co-Creation with Generative AI: Reconciling Parallel Thinking Channels, Intuition, and Epistemic Transformation in Higher Education
papers.summary: AI as a cognitive partner whose knowledge disagreements can enhance learning and intellectual development rather than merely as a technological instrument. This research paper combines theories of dialogic pedagogy, cognitive dissonance, and epistemic humility via conceptual analysis. It looks at how Parallel Thinking Channels promote critical thinking, introspection, and the innovative combination of computational reasoning with human intuition. The purpose of this study is to advance the concept of dialogic cocreation by examining the revolutionary potential of generative AI in higher education portrays. This study utilized a quantitative approach with 419 undergraduate and post-graduate students as participants. The data analysis, conceptual model and hypotheses were evaluated employing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8 to analyse the associations between the constructs of the study. The results of study show that the disparities arising from the conflict between machine-generated results and human reasoning serve as triggers for transformative learning. By merging intuition with computational thinking, students enhance their ability to manage uncertainty, broaden their understanding, and cultivate flexible intellectual resilience.
